entries.title: a mass-balanced reaction named DM_atp(c) is classified as an exchange
entries.why: SExRxnBoolHeuristic is built at line 170 before the ATP removals; line 198 clears it with the bool of line 189 (DM_atp_c_ only), so DM_atp(c) and ATPM stay external in SIntRxnBool (line 256) although the code/messages (lines 176, 184) say they should be internal.

entries.title: a model without c gets a c with one entry per metabolite
entries.why: Line 68 sets model.c = zeros(nMet,1) while the header (line 19) documents an n x 1 vector created as zeros; the returned model carries an m x 1 c.

entries.title: the exchange prefix Ex_ is never recognised
entries.why: Lines 159 and 162 use strncmp('Ex_', rxns, 5), which can never match a 3-character prefix followed by other characters; line 42 documents Ex_ as an exchange prefix.

entries.title: the biomass reaction found from biomassRxnAbbr is printed at every printLevel
entries.why: Line 98 fprintf is not guarded by printLevel, unlike every other message; output only.

entries.title: Every formula stops with an error because the group name FULLR2 contains a digit
entries.why: Line 14 lists 'FULLR2'/'FULLR3' and line 17 passes them as element; numAtomsOfElementInFormula line 26-28 errors on any non-letter in element before its FULLR translation (lines 61-63), so every call fails.

entries.title: The default of massImbalance uses nRxn before it is defined
entries.why: Line 57 uses nRxn, which is first assigned at line 72, so every call without the optional massImbalance errors.

entries.title: A proton-driven reaction uses an undefined or stale proton index
entries.why: In the proton-transport branch (lines 213-248) indexHRxn is never computed (its assignment at 230 is commented out); line 248 uses the value left from line 270 of an earlier reaction, or errors if none.

entries.title: The missing-formula warning tests the whole formula list
entries.why: Line 108 strcmp(model.metFormulas,'') is a vector, so with some (not all) empty formulas line 115 calls numAtomsOfElementInFormula('', 'H'), which indexes formula(1) at its line 38 and errors; the unreached handling at lines 109-113 shows partial missing formulas are an intended input, so the caller gets an error, not just a missing warning.

entries.title: The report file is never closed
entries.why: Line 124 fopen with no fclose anywhere in the function; a leaked handle does not change the returned model.

notes: Entry 3 is under-rated: a model with some empty metFormulas errors at numAtomsOfElementInFormula line 38 (formula(1) of ''), not merely loses a warning.

entries.title: A results model without balancedRxnBool stops with an error
entries.why: Line 194 does fail when the field is absent, but the premise is wrong: checkModelProperties (line 204-205) calls findStoichConsistentSubset with massBalanceCheck=1, which sets model.balancedRxnBool (findStoichConsistentSubset lines 181-216), so the documented input (output of checkModelProperties) has the field; a model without it is outside the documented input.

notes: Quarantine rests only on the claim that checkModelProperties never sets balancedRxnBool, which the code contradicts. The isfield check at lines 184-188 is a mild sign absence was anticipated; a run of checkModelProperties on a small model would settle it.

entries.title: The fraction of stoichiometrically consistent rows is inverted
entries.why: Line 75 computes size(S,1)/nnz(SConsistentMetBool) (>= 1), so the test < 0.60 at line 76 never holds and sufficientlyStochConsistent (used at line 176) never flags a model; line 78 would also read modelResults(j).modelID instead of .model.modelID.

entries.title: The entropy maximiser is resolved only to the pdco optimality tolerance
entries.why: Mechanism is real: alpha = 1e-6 (line 51) makes the gradient alpha*log(x) of order 1e-7, below pdco's default FeaTol/OptTol 1e-6 (pdcoSet lines 114-115; line 34 keeps defaults), so pdco stops far from the minimiser. Whether an approximate m within the solver's own tolerances contradicts the documented 'primal solution' is a judgment: bool (m>0) and the only caller's use (checkStoichiometricConsistency line 335-341, m>epsilon) are unaffected because interior-point x is always positive. A documented accuracy requirement, or a caller whose result changes, would decide it.

entries.title: printLevel is ignored and pdco always prints its iteration log
entries.why: options.Print = printLevel-1 is commented out (line 42) and pdcoSet default Print = 1; output only.

notes: Not established as quarantining. Separate latent issue: pdcoObj line 74 obj = alpha*x'*(log(x)-x) is sum(x log x - x^2), inconsistent with the gradient alpha*log(x) at line 75 (should be x'*log(x) - sum(x)).

entries.title: The balance check prints ans = [] for every new reaction
entries.why: Line 142 showprogress(i/S_nrxns(1)) has no semicolon and showprogress returns fout (= [] in that path, showprogress line 24); output only.

entries.title: The missing-formula message is never shown; an empty formula raises an index error
entries.why: Line 117 isempty(newrxns(i,3)) tests a 1x1 cell and is never true, so the handling at 118-122 is unreachable; LoadReaction then returns cell(0,6) for '' (LoadReaction lines 31-33, 79) and line 144 meta_meta{1} errors.

entries.title: A metabolite without charged formula raises an error after BalancePrep's message
entries.why: BalancePrep lines 28-33 shows a msgbox and returns [] for an empty charged formula; ReactionChecks line 150 then does output{3} on [] and errors instead of returning [] as its header (line 22) intends.

entries.title: A new reaction identical to a database reaction leaves an empty row in data
entries.why: Lines 318-319 write data{i,...} for sims row i only in the non-equal branch, so a row whose reaction is in equality (removed at 329) stays empty when a later row is filled; the gap is in an auxiliary display structure.

entries.title: Elements outside the fixed list of twelve are not checked
entries.why: Line 26 hard-codes 12 elements and lines 31-43 count only those, so a reaction unbalanced only in Na, K, Cl, Ca, etc. returns [] (lines 50-58), contradicting the documented 'empty if balance checks out' (line 14); the header names no element restriction.

entries.title: A numeric literal ID is not deleted
entries.why: AndNode line 38 calls LiteralNode.contains, which uses strcmp(self.id, literal) (LiteralNode line 62), false for a numeric literal; Node.m line 78 documents 'As string or number', so deleteLiteral(1) silently does nothing.

entries.title: convertToDNF of an AndNode without children stops with an error
entries.why: With no children, sizes is empty, line 125 step = ones(0,1), isValid is true and nextcombination line 189 indexes combination(1) of an empty vector; an empty AndNode is not a defined input.

entries.title: removeDuplicateLiterals removes the wrong children when a child that is not a literal comes before a literal
entries.why: Line 199 unique returns positions within the literal subset, but line 200 setdiff compares them with positions among all children (line 197), so with [L1, And, L2] child 3 (L2) is removed, and with [And, L1, L1] both literals are removed.

entries.title: isequal is false for a tree with a repeated clause, and not symmetric
entries.why: After the first loop empties geneSets, the loop at 360-377 never removes from otherGeneSets and line 363-365 breaks with setFound false, so any leftover duplicate clause of otherNode gives false; the reverse call succeeds via presentsets (347-353).

entries.title: isequal is false for equivalent trees with different literals
entries.why: Lines 321-326 return false when the literal sets differ and lines 331-359 compare DNF clauses without absorption, while the header (lines 318-319) promises equality of truth tables; x1 or (x1 and x2) == x1 is not recognised.

entries.title: contains stops with an error on a node without children
entries.why: Lines 167-173 assign res only inside the loop, so an empty node leaves res unassigned; an empty node is not a defined input.

entries.title: The rules are not reduced to the minimal DNF form: absorbed clauses are kept
entries.why: Lines 31-37 do reduce, convertToDNF and removeDNFduplicates, which only drops identical literal sets (OrNode lines 86-94); no absorption step exists, so 'x(1) | (x(1) & x(2))' is not reduced to x(1) as the header (lines 2, 15) promises.

entries.title: A numeric literal ID is not deleted
entries.why: Line 138 uses LiteralNode.contains (strcmp on the char id), so a numeric literalID, documented in Node.m line 78, never matches and deleteLiteral(1) has no effect.

entries.title: convertToCNF of an OrNode without children returns an empty AndNode, which evaluates to true, while the empty OrNode evaluates to false
entries.why: Lines 31-38 return AndNode() unchanged when there are no children; AndNode.evaluate starts true (AndNode line 15) and OrNode.evaluate false (line 16). Empty nodes are undefined input.

entries.title: metSBOTerms and geneSBOTerms are created as rows, not m x 1 and g x 1
entries.why: Lines 33 and 38 grow a new cell with {i}, which creates a 1 x m / 1 x g row; only rxnSBOTerms is converted with columnVector (line 84), while the OUTPUT (lines 21-24) documents m x 1 and g x 1.

entries.title: Every call stops because parseSimPhenyGPRA does not exist
entries.why: Line 24 calls parseSimPhenyGPRA; no file of that name exists anywhere in the repository (searched src, external, all paths), so every call errors.

entries.title: Every call stops because parseSimPhenyGPRA does not exist
entries.why: Line 23 calls parseSimPhenyGPRA, which is not defined anywhere in the repository, so every call errors.

entries.title: The documented constraint index cannot be used as constraintID
entries.why: The validator at line 52 requires ischar(x), so a numeric index (documented at lines 25-26, and handled by the ischar test at line 75) is rejected by parser.parse.

entries.title: The documented variable index cannot be used as variableID
entries.why: Line 32 validator requires ischar(x), rejecting the numeric index documented at lines 14-15.

entries.title: The documented option Name stops with an error
entries.why: Lines 51-54 build the field name ['evar' varargin{i}] = 'evarName', but addCOBRAVariables stores names in evarNames (addCOBRAVariables lines 122-136), so model.evarName errors.

entries.title: With one metabolite to change, the random selection reduces the S row to a scalar
entries.why: For one metabolite model.S(OldMetInd,:) is a row, and all()/any() at lines 63-64 reduce along dimension 2 to a scalar, so find returns 1 or [] instead of reaction indices.

entries.title: The extra reactions are drawn from a set that already contains the selected ones
entries.why: Line 72 draws Rxn-numel(RxnsIndAll) from RxnsIndAny, which includes RxnsIndAll, and union drops repeats, so fewer than Rxn reactions can be modified; line 67 double-counts the same reactions.

entries.title: A partly unknown reaction list is not reported
entries.why: Line 54 min(RxnsInd == 0) is true only if all are missing; with one missing, changeMets indexes S(:,0) (line 86) and errors with a generic indexing message instead of the intended one. The caller gets an error either way on an invalid input.

entries.title: custom fields named after the type are missed for a model with one or no element of that type
entries.why: Line 104 uses length(type-1), i.e. the full length of 'rxns', so 'rxnCustom' fails the prefix test and is dropped at lines 105-108; the comment and line 184 (length(type)-1) show the intended 'rxn' prefix, and the header documents rxnXYZ fields as associated.

entries.title: Two models with different numbers of reactions stop with an error
entries.why: Line 109 value1 == value2 on numeric fields of different sizes and line 121 strcmp on cell arrays of different sizes error; nothing checks sizes first, though comparing two models is the documented purpose.

entries.title: Logical fields are never compared
entries.why: Lines 108-124 handle only isnumeric, iscellstr and ischar; a logical field matches none, nDiff stays 0, and isSame is true despite differing common fields (OUTPUT line 16).

entries.title: Text fields are compared with every non-word character removed, not only white space
entries.why: Lines 104-105 regexprep(value,'[^\w'']','') strip all non-word characters, so 'R-1' equals 'R1'; the comment at line 102 says only whitespace is removed.

entries.title: The message for differing nested subSystems names prints 0 positions
entries.why: Line 86 prints nDiff(i) before line 88 assigns it; message only.

entries.title: Annotating a reaction of a standard COBRA model stops with an error
entries.why: contructItems (lines 451-467) indexes every n-row field with model.(f)(num), which fails for a 2x0 rxnGeneMat, and applies strrep (lines 465-467) to numeric and nested-cell fields such as subSystems; a standard createModel model therefore errors.

entries.title: A reaction listed by an ID in the last row of r_info.ID is not coloured
entries.why: Lines 110-118 use strict tests id < m and id > rr*m && id < (rr+1)*m (m, n left over from lines 74-75), so a linear index in the last row (e.g. 6 for a 2x3 array) never maps to column 1 and the reaction is reported missing (line 128-131).

entries.title: The html colours of the second column of listRxn_Color are ignored
entries.why: Line 38-39 length(size(...)) is always >= 2, so p = 0 and listColor (line 180) is never used; the documented second column of html colours (lines 15-16) has no effect.

entries.title: The second output is not assigned when no listed link has a non-zero width
entries.why: listRxnColour is assigned only at lines 175-176 when w ~= 0; with no such link, requesting the documented second output errors.

entries.title: Reaction IDs with (e) are not converted to the _e field name
entries.why: Line 142 replaces '(e)' only when isempty(strfind(newRxnName,'(e)')), i.e. when there is none; the condition is inverted, so R_EX_glc(e) is looked up and the width is not set.

entries.title: A reaction whose structure field is named by the reaction ID itself is left unchanged
entries.why: When isfield(ref, listRxn{r}) at line 140 holds, the else branch does nothing (newRxnName = listRxn{r} is commented out at line 137), so such reactions keep their width despite the documented purpose.

entries.title: Every matched species receives the MIRIAM entries of the last infix entry
entries.why: The loop at 280-303 has no break, so after it in = length(rxnName); line 327 constructItems(infix(in), ...) always uses the last entry, while line 289 uses the matched one for the rdf:about.

entries.title: The documented option miriam_path stops with an error
entries.why: miriam is loaded only inside if nargin<7 (lines 50-60); passing miriam_path (documented line 36) leaves miriam undefined at line 327.

entries.title: A parsed model with no reaction found in the COBRA model raises an error
entries.why: rea_M is created only inside the found branch (lines 142-183) and read unconditionally at line 217, so a valid comparison with no matches errors instead of filling listOfNotFound.

entries.title: An attribute name that occurs more than once in the line stops the function
entries.why: Line 21 keeps every strfind match, so 'id' (also inside 'metaid') gives a vector p_st (line 23) and the colon at line 25 fails; CellDesigner lines routinely carry both metaid and id.

entries.title: Debug output of the start index, the rest of the line and the end index
entries.why: Line 23 lacks a semicolon and lines 27 and 34 disp debug values; output only.

entries.title: A one-column para stops with an error at the default colour
entries.why: Line 39 sets '#FF0000FF', which contains 'FF' twice, so line 58 st = [2 8] and color(st+2:end) at line 60 errors; the one-column case is explicitly handled at lines 38-39.

entries.title: A colour code without '#' or 'FF' in the first row stops with an error
entries.why: When line 43 is false, line 48 sets s = 1 and line 52 reads para{rr-1,1} = para{0,1}; a plain hex triplet is the documented colour format (lines 11-13).

entries.title: A '#RRGGBB' colour containing 'FF' is truncated
entries.why: Lines 57-60 strip everything up to the first 'FF' in any colour longer than 6 characters, so '#00FF00' becomes '00' and then '#00'.

entries.title: Reactions without expressed genes keep weight 0 when any reaction is inconsistent
entries.why: Line 104 isEmptyFirstColumn(i) & model.SConsistentRxnBool yields an n-vector; if is false whenever one entry is false, so the median replacement (comment line 102) never happens for models with an inconsistent reaction.

entries.title: A model without SConsistentRxnBool fails before the function's own check
entries.why: Line 35 reads model.SConsistentRxnBool before the check at line 39; either way the call errors, only the message differs.

entries.title: The maxThickness input is ignored
entries.why: Line 46 tests exist('thickness','var'), which is always false at that point, so line 47 overwrites any maxThickness passed (documented line 35).

entries.title: The largest flux gets line width 0 and the smallest the maximum width
entries.why: normalizeFluxes lines 136-140 return thickness*(1 - (f-min)/range), so the largest |flux| gets 0 and the smallest the maximum, contrary to useThickness 'change thickness according to the flux' (line 50) and the 'range of 1 to 10' comment (line 129).

entries.title: The overlay content is truncated to 'name' before it is sent
entries.why: Line 54 sprintf(content) treats the URL-encoded '%09r...' as a format specifier ('%09' then invalid conversion 'r'), so output stops after 'name'; buildFluxDistLayout comments the same sprintf out (its line 120).

entries.title: fluxMap holds the widths of the input map, not the flux widths
entries.why: Line 88 builds fluxMap from map.rxnWidth (the input) instead of map2.rxnWidth set at lines 79-86, so the documented width values (line 31) are not returned.

entries.title: A flux vector of zeros gives NaN widths
entries.why: An all-zero fbaSolution.v is a valid documented input (n x 1 flux vector); line 62 divides by max = 0, giving NaN widths, while lines 70 and 82 show the intent that non-carrying reactions get width 1. Not an undocumented input, so not a limitation.

entries.title: A flux of exactly 1e-3 of the largest flux keeps width 0.001
entries.why: Lines 69-70 use > 1e-3 and < 1e-3, so a ratio of exactly 1e-3 keeps the raw ratio as its width; the caller receives a width outside the band set, which changes the result, not just documentation (minor boundary case).

notes: Entries 2 and 3 are real; by the rule they change what the caller gets on valid input, so they are wrong-result rather than limitation/cosmetic. Quarantine is already supported by entry 1.

entries.title: Numeric reaction IDs of different lengths do not match the map
entries.why: Line 45 cellstr(num2str(reactionIDs)) pads shorter numbers on the left (' 1'), and cellstr strips only trailing blanks, so ID '1' never matches map.rxnName; the conversion is deliberate (lines 43-45).

entries.title: Subsystems stored as cells of cells raise an error
entries.why: Line 105 char(model.subSystems(idsModel)) fails on a cell containing a cell; nested subSystems is the current COBRA format (as createModel writes it).

entries.title: Numeric confidence scores are written as control characters
entries.why: Line 102 char(model.rxnConfidenceScores(idsModel)) converts a number to its character code (char(3)); rxnConfidenceScores is a numeric field by the COBRA field definitions.

entries.title: A metabolite shown twice in the map gets its note twice in each copy
entries.why: listmets (line 50) contains the duplicated name twice and each pass of the branch at lines 67-76 appends to every copy, so each copy holds the summary twice; note text only.

entries.title: The optional areaWidth is not defaulted when areaHeight is given
entries.why: The default areaWidth (line 27) is nested inside if nargin < 3 (line 24), so a three-argument call leaves areaWidth unset and line 42 errors.

entries.title: The default colour 'Red' is not a key of createColorsMap
entries.why: Line 32 sets color = 'Red' while createColorsMap keys are upper case ('RED'), so colors(color) at line 49 errors whenever the documented default (line 20, 'RED') is used and a protein matches.

entries.title: Reactions with several subsystems shift the selection to the wrong reactions
entries.why: Line 45 flattens [model.subSystems{:}], whose length differs from rxns when a reaction has several subsystems (or for char subsystems, which concatenate to one char row), so the logical index misaligns or exceeds model.rxns.

entries.title: Secondary reaction lines are coloured with the undefined function Colors
entries.why: Lines 36 and 42 call Colors(color); no Colors function exists in src or external, so any map with the complete structure (rxnReactantLineColor present) errors.

entries.title: An included species named as an ion makes the main species of the same index an ION
entries.why: Line 166 writes newmap.specType{m} with m indexing specIncName (line 162); lines 188-190 show the intended specIncType for included species.

entries.title: A single reaction name found once leaves the output rxnIDref unassigned
entries.why: In the char branch (lines 26-34) rxnIDref is set only when no match (line 29) or several matches (line 33); a single match leaves the documented output unassigned.

entries.title: A list with a reaction name absent from the map is an error
entries.why: Line 23 ismember returns 0 for an absent name and line 24 map.rxnID(rxnID) indexes with 0; the char form returns 0 for an absent name, so absent names are anticipated.

entries.title: Fails instead of returning empty lists when no listed reaction is in the map
entries.why: formulaList and rxnsList are assigned only inside the loop over PresentRxns (lines 99-100); with none present the outputs are unassigned, though absent reactions are announced at line 41 and returned as absentRxns.

entries.title: The help text describes absentRxns as reactions of the map not in the model
entries.why: Line 30 says 'Reactions in the map not in the model' but line 38 computes setdiff(rxnList, map.rxnName); documentation only.

entries.title: The complex aliases and complex species of the map are not written
entries.why: Lines 123-124 assign xmlStruct values into the local map (map.complexAlias{k} = xmlStruct...) instead of the reverse, so edited complex aliases/IDs are never written.

entries.title: A map with exactly one complex or one included species cannot be written
entries.why: Lines 89, 106, 123, 143 and 159 brace-index lists that xml2struct returns as a struct for a single element; lines 272-274 handle that case only for compartments. xmlStruct is documented as xml2struct output.

entries.title: Included species without notes are written with empty notes
entries.why: Line 148 tests ~isempty(map.specIncNotes) (the whole list) rather than the entry, so an empty notes element is written; content differs only by an empty element.

entries.title: The run time is printed on every call
entries.why: tic at line 84 and toc without output at line 287 print the elapsed time; output only.

entries.title: A map with exactly one complex species alias cannot be read
entries.why: Lines 99, 118, 140, 171 and 194 brace-index lists that xml2struct returns as a struct when there is one element; lines 344-346 handle exactly that case for compartments only.

entries.title: Reaction notes written inside XHTML elements cannot be read
entries.why:
Line 334 reads notes.html.body.Text unconditionally; when the body holds a

element there is no Text field, while the species branch guards it (lines 124-127).

entries.title: The run time is printed on every call
entries.why: tic at line 91 and bare toc at line 360; output only.

entries.title: The field compartName is missing for a map without compartments
entries.why: Line 357 sets only map.compartAlias = '' when there are no compartment aliases, so the documented output field compartName ('empty if no info', line 87) is absent.

entries.title: Secondary links are recoloured by position, not by the index of the non-empty entries
entries.why: Lines 51-60 and 67-76 loop t/r = 1:length(index) and index entry t/r instead of index(t)/index(r), so non-empty secondary links not at the start are never recoloured, contrary to the OUTPUT (lines 24-26).
